CS16.question: Kabir is 16. If he says he's 18 to skip the parent check, what happens?
options: He's safer, because he's treated like an adult
He loses the protections meant for children
CS16.explanation: Under 18, apps can't track his behaviour or target ads at him. Lying about his age switches that off.

LS17.question: Can Meera, Kabir's adult sister, give consent for PlayVerse to process his data?
LS17.modelAnswer: No. s. 9(1) requires the verifiable consent of the parent (including a lawful guardian, by the Explanation). Under s. 2(j)(i), where the Data Principal is a child, the term includes her parents or lawful guardian, not siblings or other relatives. Rule 10(1) requires PlayVerse to check that the person identifying as the parent is an identifiable adult. Claiming to be Kabir's parent would mean giving false details, contrary to s. 15(b), the duty not to impersonate another person.

CS19.question: Who can agree to an app using a child's data?
CS19.explanation: Anyone under 18 is a child, and only a parent or lawful guardian can give consent, after the app checks they're a real adult.

LS18.question: Kabir's mother has no PlayVerse account. How must PlayVerse check she is an adult who can consent?
shortAnswerOptions: Ask her to tick "I am over 18"
Use reliable identity and age details, or a virtual token from an authorised entity such as a DigiLocker provider
LS18.modelAnswer: Rule 10(1) requires due diligence that the parent is an identifiable adult, by reference to (a) reliable identity and age details the fiduciary already holds, or (b) details she voluntarily provides, directly or through a virtual token issued by an authorised entity. Rule 10(2) defines "adult" as 18 or over and includes DigiLocker service providers as authorised sources. Rule 10's Illustration, Case 2, is this exact situation: a child declares a parent who has no account.

CS17.question: Kabir's mother agreed to PlayVerse. Can it now show him ads based on how he plays?
options: No, targeted ads at children aren't allowed
CS17.explanation: Even with a parent's consent, apps can't track a child's behaviour or aim ads at them.

LS19.question: Kabir's parent consented. Can PlayVerse use his play-time data for targeted Gem Pack offers and a public top-spenders leaderboard?
LS19.modelAnswer: No. s. 9(3) bars tracking or behavioural monitoring of children and targeted advertising directed at them. Parental consent under s. 9(1) does not lift this bar. s. 9(2) separately bars processing likely to cause any detrimental effect on a child's well-being, which late-night spending prompts and a public spending leaderboard arguably are. The only exemptions from s. 9(1) and 9(3) are the classes and purposes in the Fourth Schedule (s. 9(4) read with Rule 12) and a Central Government notification for verifiably safe processing (s. 9(5)). None covers a game's advertising. Breach of s. 9 is Schedule item 3: up to ₹200 crore.

CS18.question: When can an app track a child's live location?
options: Only to keep the child safe
CS18.explanation: The Rules allow live location tracking of a child only for that child's safety and protection.

LS20.question: PlayVerse says the Rules let it track Kabir's live location for "Find a Teammate". Is it right?
LS20.modelAnswer: No. Fourth Schedule Part B, item 4, exempts processing "for the determination of real-time location of a child" only on the condition that it is restricted to tracking her location "in the interest of her safety and protection or security". Matchmaking players serves neither. The other location exemptions belong to educational institutions, crèches and child-care centres, and school transport (Part A, items 3–5), which PlayVerse is not. Location tracking for a game feature therefore falls under the s. 9(3) bar on tracking children.

CF19.title: Who counts as a child
CF19.plain: Anyone under 18 is a child under the law. Their parents or lawful guardian act for them.

CF20.title: A parent's real OK
CF20.plain: Before using a child's data, an app must get a parent's consent and check that the parent is a real adult, using details it already holds or ID such as DigiLocker.

CF21.title: No tracking, no targeted ads
CF21.plain: Apps can't track or monitor how children behave, aim ads at them, or do anything likely to harm their well-being, even with a parent's consent.

CF22.title: The narrow exceptions
CF22.plain: Hospitals, schools, crèches and school transport get limited exceptions, and live location tracking of a child is allowed only to keep that child safe.

endings.title: Level up
endings.caption: PlayVerse turned off location tracking for every under-18 account.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: No shortcuts, and you stood up for every kid on that app.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: You won in the end. But faking an age or a parent switches off the very protections you just fought for.

endings.title: Half a win
endings.caption: The gem offers stopped, but PlayVerse still tracks Kabir's live location.

card.title: What Meera could still do
items: Tell PlayVerse the location exemption is only for a child's safety.
Complain to the Data Protection Board if PlayVerse won't fix it.
